ai.description: This 25–30 mm frog is brown with a distinct, pale cream-colored snout. It features a granular dorsum, prominent femoral glands, and lacks webbing on the toes. It is endemic to the Western Ghats.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus webilla* is best distinguished by the presence of prominent, elongated, and pointed dermal appendages on the tips of its third and fourth fingers.
ai.habitat: The Kadalar night frog inhabits mid-elevation evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found along rocky streams at altitudes between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Kadalar night frog is strictly nocturnal, remaining hidden under rocks or vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nyctibatrachus webilla* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying terrestrial clutches of 20–30 eggs on rocks near streams, which undergo direct development.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nyctibatrachus webilla* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it inhabits mid-to-high elevation streams.
ai.callDescription: The Kadalar Night Frog produces a series of high-pitched, insect-like "ticking" chirps, typically heard while perched on mossy rocks near fast-flowing forest streams.
